title: sinewave-burst-replay-scratch-cleo
content:
Quick context
- Goal: probe how periodic (sine-like) arrival patterns interact with batching and kv-cache warmup. Trying to reproduce an odd p99 amplification we saw during a customer demo (irregular tails when load oscillates).
- Hypothesis: harmonic alignment between slot-slicing interval + batch-formation window and ingress oscillation frequencies can create constructive interference, amplifying tail latency.

Experiment setup (replay harness)
- Replayer: local harness (python) with jitter, uses timestamped traces scaled to target QPS.
- Workload: 50% short prompts (~40 tokens), 50% long (~350 tokens) to exercise kv cache reuse.
- Arrival pattern: base QPS=180, sine amplitude=±60, period sweep: [2s, 5s, 12s, 30s]. Added small gaussian jitter (sigma=20ms) to avoid perfect sync.
- Targets: measure p50/p95/p99 latency of generation latency (server side), end-to-end wall time, and batch size distribution.
- Env: dedicated dev pool (A100s), model x-small-8q (quantized test), runtime commit: a7f3b9
- Repeats: 6 runs per period, warm/cold cache variants (cold = flush kv between runs)

Raw observations summary
- Period=2s: relatively stable; p95 ~ 75ms, p99 ~ 210ms. Batch sizes centered at 6.
- Period=5s: noticeable spikes; intermittent p99s up to 520ms correlated with batch sizes jumping to 20-30 for a short window.
- Period=12s: strong resonance events every ~12s window: p99 median ~680ms, worst ~1.1s. Batch formation showed synchronized queuing (many requests arrive near same phase).
- Period=30s: lower average but occasional mega-batches when sine crest aligned with autoscaler step — p99 ~420ms.
- Cold vs warm cache: cold runs increased p50 by ~12ms and p99 by ~80ms on average, but the resonance amplification factor (ratio of resonant p99 to baseline p99) was larger in warm runs (~3.2x) vs cold (~2.1x).

Detailed notes / traces
- Trace 2025-10-20-run-5 (period=12s, warm): saw a consistent pattern where batch sizes ramp from 6 -> 18 in ~120ms, then several tokens of generation incur KV fetch stalls due to cache miss propagation when many sessions are activated simultaneously.
- Queue trace shows enqueued timestamps tightly clustered within 30ms.
- When slot-slice window (batch flush interval) = 25ms, resonance is worst. Increasing to 40ms smoothed batches but raised median latency ~8ms.

Quick hypotheses (why this happens)
1) Harmonic alignment: when arrival period is an integer multiple of the slot window, arrivals land in the same phase repeatedly -> massive short-term concurrency -> oversized batches that push GPU memory/dispatch scheduling.
2) KV-cache priming: warm caches make long prompts more cache-friendly, so when bursts hit, the effective work per request increases (long contexts get prefilled), increasing per-batch compute and queueing latency. In cold runs this effect is dampened because everything misses and costs are more uniform.
3) Autoscaler/slot interplay: autoscaler step latency (60s granularity in this pool) can create a slow ramp; if a long-period crest coincides with a transient capacity increase, queuing patterns amplify before capacity stabilizes.

Small experiments tried (quick A/B)
- Increased batching timeout from 25ms -> 40ms: reduced p99 spikes for period=12s but moved some tail mass to p95 (tradeoff).
- Added exponential jitter on ingress (random up to ±150ms): smoothed the big spikes significantly; p99 reduced ~45% in resonant runs.
- Disabled slot-aligned batching (fallback to dynamic batching): eliminated the worst megabatches but increased CPU overhead slightly.

Open questions / followups
- Need to measure impact at higher base QPS (400) and smaller amplitude (±30) — will harmonic effects persist?
- Is there a cheap runtime heuristic to detect resonant ingress (autocorrelation peak at batching window) and introduce micro-jitter?
- Should we expose a per-tenant jitter knob in Redwood Dedicated? Would help high-sensitivity customers.
- How does this behave with multi-tenant noise? current runs are single-tenant; cross-tenant alignment might be rarer but possible.

Immediate next steps (TODOs)
- [ ] Run 400 QPS baseline sweep (periods 5s,12s,30s) week of 2025-11-04 (assigned: Arjun).
- [ ] Add instrumentation: record batch-formation phase histogram relative to sine phase (Lina) — need a small patch in replayer + runtime hook.
- [ ] Try adaptive micro-jitter in replayer to quantify smoothing benefit (Cleo).
- [ ] Draft a short note for SRE/Autoscale team describing observed interplay with step-scaling (link PR).

Notes-to-self (brain dump)
- If we can detect resonance cheaply (autocorrelation in 10s window), we could apply tiny randomized offsets per request to break alignment; likely low perf cost and big tail benefit.
- Consider adding a "burst-smoothing" policy in Redwood Console: when chosen, throttle small slices or inject jitter at proxy layer for tenant. Need product consult.

References / links in experiment logs
- slack thread: #runtime-bench -> https://slack.redwood/channels/runtime-bench (see messages Oct20)
- linear ticket: RED-1423 (linked above)

Bottom line (rough)
- Periodic ingress patterns can produce outsized p99 due to constructive alignment with batch windows. Easy mitigations (micro-jitter, wider batching window, dynamic batching) all help but trade off median latency or CPU. For customer-facing mitigation, recommend a per-tenant micro-jitter toggle plus monitoring alert on batch-size distribution skew.

End of scratchpad.

-- cleo
